questions: Is the signal smooth and monotonic across the line offset range, or does it saturate or dead-zone at the edges of the array?
Does the line get lost on any track (sum of readings below 0.05), and at which bend types?
Is steering jitter (steering_oscillation) caused by sensor noise or by geometry such as sensor spacing or forward offset?
Would a longer or shorter wheel track or lower mass make the controller easier to tune?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: Tell me if a wider or narrower array, or a larger or smaller footprint, would make the controller simpler.

intent: Baseline symmetric five-sensor array with sensors spaced 1 cm apart across the line, 5 cm ahead of the axle, using 12 mm footprints so that adjacent sensors overlap the tape edge. Weights are linear in x so the signal is antisymmetric and fully proportional to lateral offset. The aim is a stable, complete run and a clean measurement baseline. The Integrator should report how the array behaves under their controller so I can tune spacing, size and forward position next.
learning: No evidence yet. Baseline hypotheses: (1) a 4 cm array with 12 mm footprints gives a monotonic signal over roughly ±1.5 cm of offset; (2) a forward offset of 5 cm gives enough lead to reduce oscillation at speed; (3) the 0.12 m body and 0.0625 m off-track limit leave enough margin that the tape is not the limiting factor. Measurements to check next: rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, completion_time, steering_oscillation and progress on every development track.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or integration feedback, so this is a baseline, not an optimised design. I chose a symmetric five-sensor bar that spans about 4 cm across the 25 mm tape, so the line stays under at least one sensor through a moderate bend. The 12 mm footprint is half the tape width, so neighbouring sensors overlap the tape edge and give a graded reading. Sensors sit 5 cm ahead of the axle to read the line before the wheels reach it. Weights are proportional to sensor x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so a positive weight on the left sensor steers left, matching the signal convention. Body and wheels are mid-range to keep the yaw inertia and drive torque moderate: 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius, 0.12 m body width (off-track limit about 0.0625 m, which gives margin), 0.18 m body length, 0.8 kg mass. I expect a complete run with a moderate rms error, which I will check against the race telemetry.
